data.name: Metadata_Overview_Item_BaseController
data.value: Base controller support: GCFoundationBaseController collects per-page meta tags and exposes them to views via ViewData["MetaTags"] after each action.

data.name: Metadata_Overview_Item_TypedModel
data.value: Strongly-typed model: MetaTag supports name/content, property/content (Open Graph, Twitter), http-equiv/content, charset, and optional English/French strings via contentEn / contentFr with content as fallback.

data.name: Metadata_Overview_Item_LayoutMerge
data.value: Layout rendering and merge: _FoundationLayout.cshtml merges controller-provided tags with configured global tags, avoiding duplicates by name or property. Controller tags take precedence.

data.name: Metadata_Overview_Item_Configuration
data.value: Configuration: GlobalMetaTags in GCFoundationComponentsSettings is a collection of typed MetaTag objects (appsettings.json).

data.name: Metadata_Configuration_Intro
data.value: Set global, always-on meta tags in appsettings.json using the typed MetaTag structure:

data.name: Metadata_Usage_Intro
data.value: Inherit from GCFoundationBaseController and call AddMetaTag in your action.

data.name: Metadata_Behavior_Item_Dedup
data.value: De-duplication: A tag with the same Name or Property replaces the previous one. Global tags are only added if not already present.

data.name: Metadata_Behavior_Item_Encoding
data.value: Encoding: Attributes are HTML-encoded on render.

data.name: Metadata_Behavior_Item_LocalizedContent
data.value: Localized content: Optional contentEn and contentFr are chosen from CurrentUICulture when rendering; content is the fallback and suits language-neutral values (for example charset, og:type).

data.name: Metadata_Behavior_Item_Attributes
data.value: Attributes: Use either Name or Property (not both). Charset is standalone; HttpEquiv generally pairs with Content.

data.name: Metadata_Behavior_Item_Order
data.value: Render order: Controller tags render first, then non-duplicated global tags.

data.name: Metadata_Behavior_Item_NoViewChanges
data.value: No view changes needed: The layout picks up ViewData["MetaTags"] automatically.

data.name: Metadata_Notes_Item_BaseClass
data.value: Base class requirement: Controllers must inherit GCFoundationBaseController to use AddMetaTag.

data.name: Metadata_Notes_Item_OptionalSection
data.value: Optional section: @section Metas { ... } remains available for manual HTML if needed, but is not required.

data.name: Index_Page_Title
data.value: Installation

data.name: Index_Intro
data.value: This guide adds GCFoundation to an ASP.NET Core MVC application. The quick start gives you the Canada.ca layout (header, footer, menu, breadcrumbs and language toggle), the components and the default security policies. The optional sections then cover features you can add when you need them.

data.name: Index_SideNav_OnThisPage
data.value: On this page

data.name: Index_Prerequisites_Heading
data.value: Prerequisites

data.name: Index_Prerequisites_Item_Sdk
data.value: The .NET 10 SDK

data.name: Index_Prerequisites_Item_Ide
data.value: Visual Studio 2026 (version 18.0 or later), Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit, or another editor that supports .NET 10

data.name: Index_Prerequisites_Item_Project
data.value: An ASP.NET Core MVC project that targets net10.0. To start from scratch, run dotnet new mvc -n MyApp.

data.name: Index_Prerequisites_NuGet
data.value: GCFoundation packages are published on nuget.org, so you don't need to add a package source.

data.name: Index_QuickStart_Heading
data.value: Quick start

data.name: Index_QuickStart_Intro
data.value: Follow these steps in order. The examples use MyApp as the project name and root namespace: replace it with your own.

data.name: Index_Step1_Heading
data.value: 1. Install the packages

data.name: Index_Step1_Intro
data.value: From your project folder, add the two GCFoundation packages and the cloudscribe localization package. GCFoundation.Common and cloudscribe.Web.Navigation are installed automatically as dependencies.

data.name: Index_Step1_PackageManager
data.value: In the Visual Studio Package Manager Console, run Install-Package with the same package names instead.

data.name: Index_Step2_Heading
data.value: 2. Configure Program.cs

data.name: Index_Step2_Intro
data.value: Replace the contents of Program.cs with the following. It registers the GCFoundation services, the navigation used by the menu and breadcrumbs, and English and French request localization based on the first segment of the URL (/en/... or /fr/...).

data.name: Index_Step3_Heading
data.value: 3. Add your settings

data.name: Index_Step3_Intro
data.value: Add a FoundationComponentsSettings section to appsettings.json. To start, you only need the application name in both languages. It appears in the header, the menu and the page title.

data.name: Index_Step3_Note
data.value: Every other setting has a working default. You can add them later: the application version and footer links in this section, global files and meta tags (see the next steps), and the ContentPolicySettings, FoundationSession and AccountSettings sections.

data.name: Index_Step4_Heading
data.value: 4. Describe your navigation

data.name: Index_Step4_Intro
data.value: The layout builds the menu and the breadcrumbs from a navigation.xml file at the root of your project. Each node points to a controller action, and its text attribute is a resource key, not a label.

data.name: Index_Step4_PreservedRoute
data.value: Keep preservedRouteParameters="culture" on every node so that links stay in the current language.

data.name: Index_Step4_Resources
data.value: Then add the labels. In a Resources folder, create an empty Navigation class, a Navigation.resx file for English and a Navigation.fr.resx file for French, with the keys used in navigation.xml.

data.name: Index_Step4_ResourcesNote
data.value: The class and the files must have the same name and folder so that .NET can find the translations. If Visual Studio generated a Navigation.Designer.cs file for the English file, that generated class already does the job: don't create Navigation.cs.

data.name: Index_Step5_Heading
data.value: 5. Use the GCFoundation layout

data.name: Index_Step5_Intro
data.value: Make the GCFoundation tag helpers available to every view in Views/_ViewImports.cshtml:

data.name: Index_Step5_Layout
data.value: Then use the shared layout in Views/_ViewStart.cshtml. It provides the header, footer, menu, breadcrumbs, language toggle and all the GCDS and GCFoundation styles and scripts, so you no longer need the template's Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml.

data.name: Index_Step5_Content
data.value: Your views now contain only the page content. For example, in Views/Home/Index.cshtml:

data.name: Index_Step6_Heading
data.value: 6. Run the application

data.name: Index_Step6_Intro
data.value: Start the application and open /en or /fr. You should see the Canada.ca header with your application name, a menu built from navigation.xml, and a language toggle that switches between the English and French versions of the page.

data.name: Index_Step6_Troubleshooting
data.value: If the page has no styles, check that app.UseStaticFiles() is called. If the menu shows keys such as Nav_Home instead of labels, check that the resource files are in the same folder as the Navigation class and have the same name.

data.name: Index_Optional_Heading
data.value: Optional configuration

data.name: Index_Optional_Intro
data.value: Add these features only when your application needs them.

data.name: Index_NodeVisibility_Heading
data.value: Show a node in the menu or the breadcrumbs only

data.name: Index_NodeVisibility_Intro
data.value: By default, a node appears in both the menu and the breadcrumbs. Use the componentVisibility attribute to limit it to one of them: topnav for the menu, breadcrumbs for the breadcrumbs. In the menu, a node without a controller that has children is displayed as a drop-down group.

data.name: Index_NavRules_Heading
data.value: Show or hide nodes based on the user

data.name: Index_NavRules_Intro
data.value: You can hide a node unless the current request has a given claim, cookie or session value. Add a rule under the node's key in appsettings.json. Nodes without a rule are always shown.

data.name: Index_NavRules_Program
data.value: Then register the rules and the permission resolver in Program.cs, before builder.Build():

data.name: Index_NavRules_Note
data.value: Rules only hide links. They don't protect the pages: also add [Authorize] to the controllers or actions that require it.

data.name: Index_SecureCookies_Heading
data.value: Harden cookies

data.name: Index_SecureCookies_Intro
data.value: To make every cookie set by your application Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, add a cookie policy right after the language middleware:

data.name: Index_SecureCookies_Note
data.value: Secure cookies are only sent over HTTPS, so run the application with the https launch profile, including during development.

data.name: Index_ContentPolicy_Heading
data.value: Allow other content sources

data.name: Index_ContentPolicy_Intro
data.value: UseGCFoundationContentPolicies() sends a strict Content Security Policy that already allows GCFoundation, GCDS and Font Awesome. If you load scripts, styles, fonts, images, frames or API calls from other domains, list them in a ContentPolicySettings section of appsettings.json:

data.name: Index_ContentPolicy_Nonce
data.value: Inline scripts are blocked unless they carry the nonce of the current request. Add it with CspNonceHelper:

data.name: Index_UrlTranslation_Heading
data.value: Translate URLs

data.name: Index_UrlTranslation_Intro
data.value: By default, French pages use the same path as English pages (/fr/home/privacy). To give them French paths (/fr/accueil/confidentialite), install RouteLocalization.AspNetCore:

data.name: Index_UrlTranslation_AttributeRoutes
data.value: RouteLocalization works with attribute routes. Give each controller and action a route without the language: the /en and /fr prefixes are added for you.

data.name: Index_UrlTranslation_Extension
data.value: Then declare the French paths in an extension method. Routes that you don't translate keep their English path in both languages.

data.name: Index_UrlTranslation_Register
data.value: Register the extension in Program.cs before builder.Build(). Attribute-routed controllers no longer answer the site root (/), so also map it, for example to the English home page:

data.name: Index_UrlTranslation_Result
data.value: The menu, the breadcrumbs and the language toggle use the translated paths automatically.

data.name: Translations_HowToUse_Intro
data.value: Add @using GCFoundation.Components.Resources to a view, or to _ViewImports.cshtml for every view, then use the properties of the Localization class. Each property returns the term in the current language, so request localization must be configured as described in the installation quick start.
